terminal_record.title: Trump Uses “Animals” Remark During California Immigration Roundtable
terminal_record.description_short: Trump Used “Animals” Remark During May 2018 California Immigration Roundtable
terminal_record.description_medium: At a May 16, 2018, White House roundtable on sanctuary-city policies, President Donald Trump said, “These aren’t people. These are animals” after Fresno County Sheriff Margaret Mims said she knew of an MS-13 member she could not report to ICE. Trump’s reply referred broadly to “people coming into the country” without naming a group. The White House and Trump later said he meant MS-13; FactCheck.org said the original remark’s intended target could not be established with certainty.
terminal_record.description_long: On May 16, 2018, President Donald Trump held a White House roundtable with California mayors, sheriffs and other officials about sanctuary-city policies. During the discussion, Fresno County Sheriff Margaret Mims said she knew of an MS-13 member but could not tell ICE unless that person met a threshold. Trump replied that “people coming into the country” were “animals,” saying, “These aren’t people. These are animals.” In the official transcript, the remark immediately follows Mims’s reference to MS-13, but Trump’s reply does not name the gang. The White House press secretary later said Trump was referring to MS-13 gang members, and Trump said the next day that he meant MS-13. FactCheck.org reported those explanations while noting that it could not determine exactly what Trump meant in the original remark. The record should therefore describe the words and their immediate setting, then attribute the later clarification separately. It should not say the transcript proves that Trump was referring to all immigrants, or that it definitively proves he meant only MS-13. The sources establish the public remark and context; they do not document a resulting policy change or quantify harm caused by it.

source_fact_map.fact: The White House transcript dates the roundtable to May 16, 2018.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Remarks by President Trump at a California Sanctuary State Roundtable – The White House; Issued on: May 16, 2018; Cabinet Room.

source_fact_map.fact: Immediately before Trump replied, Sheriff Mims mentioned an MS-13 member she could not report to ICE below a threshold.
source_fact_map.quote: There could be an MS-13 member I know about — if they don’t reach a certain threshold, I cannot tell ICE about it.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: SHERIFF MIMS: Thank you. There could be an MS-13 member I know about — if they don’t reach a certain threshold, I cannot tell ICE about it.

source_fact_map.fact: Trump used the words 'These aren't people. These are animals' in his reply.
source_fact_map.quote: These aren’t people. These are animals.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: These aren’t people. These are animals.

source_fact_map.fact: FactCheck.org reports that the original words do not establish Trump's precise intended target.
source_fact_map.quote: We can’t say what Trump meant when he made his remarks
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: We can’t say what Trump meant when he made his remarks, but there is a history of Trump referring to MS-13 gang members as “animals.” Given that, and the larger context of the conversation about people who are in jails and in the country illegally, it’s certainly plausible that he was referring to the gang members.

source_fact_map.fact: FactCheck.org reports that the White House press secretary said Trump was referring to MS-13 gang members.
source_fact_map.quote: he “was very clearly referring to MS-13 gang members.”
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Later that day, White House Press Secretary Sarah Sanders was asked what the president meant by the remark, and she said he “was very clearly referring to MS-13 gang members.” Later that same day, Trump, too, was asked to clarify his remarks.

source_fact_map.fact: Trump's reply referred to 'people coming into the country' without naming a group in that phrase.
source_fact_map.quote: people coming into the country, or trying to come in
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: THE PRESIDENT: We have people coming into the country, or trying to come in — and we’re stopping a lot of them.

source_fact_map.fact: Trump clarified the next day that he was referring to MS-13 gangs.
source_fact_map.quote: But I’m referring, and you know I’m referring, to the MS-13 gangs that are coming in.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Later that same day, Trump, too, was asked to clarify his remarks, and he said: “But I’m referring, and you know I’m referring, to the MS-13 gangs that are coming in.”

impact_proposal.confidence_reason: The official transcript establishes the words, date, and immediate context; independent fact-checking records later clarifications but leaves original intent uncertain.
impact_proposal.rationale: This is a public remark at an immigration roundtable. No materially affected population or resulting policy, institutional, procedural, private-benefit, or persistent effect is established. Publicity alone is not affected reach.
impact_proposal.basis: One presidential statement during a California sanctuary-policy discussion; the immediate transcript context mentions MS-13, while the reply itself speaks broadly of people coming into the country.
notes: Editorial comparative estimate under impact-v2; not a measured estimate of real-world harm. Reach is kept low because the accessed sources do not quantify an affected population.
